staged_record.description_long: A New York Times report published May 20, 1981, said more than 50 well-known conservatives had convened the Council for National Policy, a new umbrella group they hoped would gain influence. Decades later, the TrumpFile page linked in this record describes a compilation of 1,011 names covering 1981 through 2020 and cautions that it may include fewer than half of the council’s members. Documented published a separate leaked September 2020 membership directory naming 426 people. Those figures describe different lists and should not be combined into a count of total members. Neither the linked compilation nor the supplied material verifies Donald Trump’s membership, position or participation in a CNP activity, and a person’s appearance in a multi-decade list would not by itself prove a role in a specific policy. The supported subject is the council’s formation and the scope and limitations of publicly available membership lists. Unless a reliable record connects Trump to the organization, this should be reframed as CNP history or excluded from a Trump-specific claim.

facts_supported: The page identifies itself as “CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy.”
The page says its compiler lists 1,011 names from 1981 through 2020 and that the list may include less than half of CNP members over the group’s 40-year existence.

The page asserts: “Before Donald Trump spoke at the last two Republican National Conventions, he read drafts of his speech to the Council for National Policy.” It also asserts that Trump told a convention audience China wanted Joe Biden to win “with the Council’s blessing.”
